site_name: Proposed Bt Street Hub On Pavement South Of Dorset House I8 And Bellwether Lane
description: Advertisement consent for two internally illuminated digital display screens, with one screen located on each side of the structure (in connection with ref: 2026/0067)
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - By reason of lack of information provided and the presence of similar 'Street Hubs' in the immediate area, the proposal is considered to constitute unnecessary street clutter that would cause harm to visual amenity and local spatial character, contrary to London Plan D8 and Local Plan Policies LP1 and LP9.

Reason : 2 - By reason of its design and siting, it is considered that the proposed Street Hub would appear as a detracting and incongruous element in the street scene, detracting from historic views and the appreciation of the adjacent heritage asset. The proposal would therefore cause less than substantial harm to the significance of the Wandsworth Town Conservation Area and less than substantial harm to the setting of the adjacent Grade II* Listed building. The public benefits of the proposal are not considered to outweigh this harm, contrary to London Plan Policy: HC1, Local Plan Policies: LP3 and LP9, Sections 66 (1) and Section 72(1) of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 and Paragraphs 200 and 201 of the NPPF.

Reason : 3 - By reason of its design, scale and siting, it is considered that the proposal would represent a safety hazard for cyclists in terms of it being an undue distraction and blocking the forward view of the cycle lane. It is therefore considered that the proposal would cause material harm to highway safety, contrary to London Plan Policy T4, LP9 and LP50.

Reason : 4 - In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive manner and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies in the Local Plan consisting of the Core Strategy, Development Management Policies Document, Supplementary Planning documents and where appropriate the Site Specific Allocations Document as well as offering a full pre application advice service. However, we have been unable to seek solutions to problems as the principle of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
